acceptanceCriteria: interop/cem01-go qualifies a linux process-containment implementation (or an explicitly bounded linux route) so verify-stable-canonical returns ACCEPT/REJECT on linux with the same verdictSha256 as native
TestTCBV0016GateVerdictRunsBothConsumers runs (not skipped) on the linux CI shard and passes
docs/specs/tasks-criterion-binding-v0.md and cem-stable-v1.md record the qualified hosts for the portable leg
body: Confirmed on 2026-10-13. interop/cem01-go qualifies process containment only in stable_process_darwin.go; stable_process_other.go answers unsupported-process-containment, so verify-stable-canonical reports outcome UNSUPPORTED on linux. The taskman cem-verdict gate (TCB-V0-016/017, PR beamfall/corvint#863) treats that as verifier-disagreement and REFUSES, which is the specified behaviour but means the gate can only GRANT on darwin. Reproduction: PR #863 CI run 38463640466, go-product-shard (0), TestTCBV0016GateVerdictRunsBothConsumers: native ACCEPT verdictSha256 14ac383d..., portable UNSUPPORTED verdictSha256 5de4c58a..., citationSha256 null. Expected: the portable consumer recomputes the same verdict on linux. Actual: UNSUPPORTED. Interim: commit d30f894fa skips the real-consumer test NOT_RUN off darwin; internal/taskman keeps the stand-in consumer on linux. The live policy v9 cem-verdict entry is required:false and the owner runs gates on darwin, so no queue impact yet.
title: cem-verdict gate cross-check: interop/cem01-go verify-stable-canonical is darwin-only, so the real-consumer leg cannot run on linux CI or any linux Tasks host
